text:
maria: Drafting a short PRD for Q3: credential surface changes. Goal is scoped API keys + RBAC primitives + org/project boundaries. Need alignment on acceptance criteria, rollout strategy, and edge cases. PRD link: https://redwood/drive/prd/cred-surface-q3

kevin: skimmed the PRD. big +1 for scoped keys. couple questions: how do we express scopes? string permissions? policy objects? also service-account UX?

ajay: from infra side: we'll need a token introspection path and a fast scope-check cache to avoid auth latency spike. naive approach: store scope blob in tokens table and cache in redis with 1s ttl. example header stays: Authorization: Bearer <token> but we should avoid new headers if possible.

sara: UX: workspace admins need a simple flow: create token -> pick projects -> pick roles -> TTL. show default "read-only" and an "advanced" mode for policy JSON. minimize clicks for devs.

maria: proposed scope model in PRD: allow two forms 1) compact role tuples e.g. project:123:reader 2) policy JSON for advanced perms. Acceptance criteria (draft):
- create/list/revoke token APIs + console flows
- token enforces project/org boundaries in runtime checks
- audit trail for token creation/use (who created, which token used by which request)
- admin can set org-level defaults (max TTL, allowed roles)
- rollout controlled by FF and offer dedicated-canary tenants first

kevin: feasibility notes: compact tuples are easiest to enforce and cheap to check. policy JSON adds complexity but we can gate it behind an "advanced" feature flag. for rollout: feature flag + canary orgs + 2-phase validation (dry-run logging then enforcement). metrics to watch: 401 spike, auth latency p95, scope-miss errors.

ajay: infra tasks rough: DB migration to tokens.scopes (jsonb), new cache path, introspection endpoint, middleware update on all ingress services. estimate: 3 sprint infra + 2 sprint app work if we parallelize. also need migration playbook to backfill existing tokens as default-global scope.

oliver: legal/compliance: confirm cross-org token use is impossible. need confirm for e-discovery: token metadata retention window. also flag any export-control concerns if tokens can allow data exfil to external integrations.

jess: sales-eng: several enterprise prospects have asked specifically for scoped keys + short TTL for SSO-less service accounts. making this GA in Q3 would unlock a couple deals; priority wise this is near-top for enterprise.

maria: edge cases I'm worried about:
- token rotation and long-running jobs (how to surface silent failures)
- tokens created via API vs console (who is the actor)
- cross-project references (embedding keys created in one project used to call another) -> should be blocked by default
- delegated scopes (user acts on behalf of another service) -> defers to an RFC if we support impersonation

kevin: rollout checklist idea:
1) design + infra + API impl behind FF
2) dry-run in prod for 2 weeks -> log scope mismatches + expose to customers via console
3) opt-in canary orgs (3 orgs) for enforcement
4) GA with org-level default controls + admin UI

ajay: plus: migration plan: create default global-scoped tokens in db for all existing tokens, mark them as legacy, and expire after 90 days if unused. provide rotate endpoint and CLI helper:
```
rwctl tokens rotate --token <id> --scope project:123:writer --ttl 24h
```
security-bot: NOTE: adding incident watch rule: monitor for >5% auth failure increase and >10ms p95 auth delta after enablement. will auto-alert #incidents and eng-oncall.

maria: asks: Kevin/Ajay/Sara/Oliver — can you comment on the PRD acceptance list above and estimate lift? I'd like a final go/no-go list for the product roadmap review on Friday. :pray:

kevin: I'll send a short RFC w/ enforcement model and perf numbers by Wed. rough estimate: MVP (compact tuples + UI flows + audit) = 6 dev-weeks. policy-json TBD.

ajay: infra estimate matches Kevin. will draft migration playbook and ops runbook.

sara: I'll mock the console flows today and post screenshots. can we aim for read-only beta by mid-August?

oliver: legal ok to proceed with safeguards; will follow up with retention policy wording.

maria: great — thanks everyone. scheduling a 30m sync Thu to lock acceptance criteria before roadmap review. tagging @kevin @ajay @sara @oliver @jess. :calendar:
